title: Two-stage MKV encode attachment preservation
summary: Implements two-stage MKV encode finalization: FFmpeg encodes video/audio/subtitles without attachment streams, then mkvmerge restores source MKV font attachments and verifies the final attachment inventory before publish.
reason: High-bitrate MKV sources with ASS font attachments were correctly routed to encode, but FFmpeg failed because the encode command mapped Matroska attachments as packet streams. The desired default is encode, with preserved ASS styling/fonts plus converted SRT fallback in the final MKV.
behavior_before: MKV encode commands included -map 0:t? and -c:t copy, causing FFmpeg to receive Matroska attachment packets and fail before encoding. ASS-to-SRT conversion could become the default subtitle even when the original styled ASS was preserved.
behavior_after: MKV encode commands leave attachments out of FFmpeg. After a successful encode, mkvmerge builds the final MKV from the encoded media plus source attachments, verifies font attachment parity, and blocks publish on mux or verification failure. Preserved ASS is default; converted SRT is embedded as a non-default fallback.
manual_validation: Synthetic two-stage MKV media validation with ffmpeg+mkvmerge - passed; final MKV had 1/1 source attachment restored plus S_TEXT/ASS and S_TEXT/UTF8 subtitle tracks.
rollback_plan: Revert the encode mux helper, module loader entry, Do-Encode mux call, failure-code additions, subtitle disposition change, dry-run two-stage command update, and related tests; then restore the prior single-stage encode command snapshots.
